title: Update on JTC's Solar Deployment Scheme and Proposal for Landlord-to-tenant Solar Energy Purchasing Guidelines
what_it_is: Update on JTC's Solar Deployment Scheme and Proposal for Landlord-to-tenant Solar Energy Purchasing Guidelines

sections.label: JTC solar deployment models
sections.summary: JTC lessees can choose between two solar deployment models that require no upfront capital outlay if JTC's appointed SolarRoof vendor is used.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Today, JTC's lessees can choose between two solar deployment models, both of which do not require any upfront capital outlay if JTC's appointed solar vendor for the SolarRoof programme is used.

sections.label: JTC mandatory solar deployment scheme
sections.summary: JTC's 2020 scheme requires lessees with new or renewed leases over 15 years and at least 800 square metres of contiguous rooftop to deploy solar.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: JTC implemented the mandatory solar deployment scheme in 2020, as highlighted by the Member.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: This scheme requires lessees with a new or renewed land lease with JTC of more than 15 years, and with at least 800 square metres of contiguous rooftop area, to carry out solar deployment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The Member will be glad to know that JTC is currently studying even more options to push solar adoption further, especially for lessees and tenants with short remaining tenures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The Government will continue to review ways to incentivise and promote more solar adoption, including co-creating solutions with private developers and industry players, as well as work with stakeholders to maximise solar energy adoption in Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore solar energy adoption
sections.summary: Solar energy is Singapore's most viable renewable energy, with deployment on track for two gigawatt peak by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Please allow me to share that solar energy is currently the most viable renewable energy in Singapore and the Government is committed to continue to accelerate our efforts to promote solar adoption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We are on track to achieving the solar panel deployment target of two gigawatt peak (GWp) by year 2030, which is equivalent powering 350,000 households annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In fact, since 2015, our solar installed capacity has increased by nine times to over 560 megawatt-peak (MWp) in the third quarter of the year 2021.

sections.label: Solar installation contracting and area
sections.summary: Typical solar installation contracting periods run between 15 and 20 years, and at least 800 square metres is required for viability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For example, as per current market practice, the typical contracting period for solar installation is between 15 years and 20 years, and a minimum of solar installation area of at least 800 square metres is required for the solar deployment for this to be viable.

sections.label: JTC SolarRoof Phase Three options
sections.summary: JTC is exploring a license fee sharing model and its SolarRoof Phase Three tender offers shorter contract options under 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And in fact, JTC is also engaging existing tenants in land-based facilities to explore the possibility of a license fee sharing model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And in addition, as part of the SolarRoof programme Phase Three tender, which was just launched in November 2021 three months ago, both rooftop licensing and solar leasing rates for shorter contract period options of less than 10 years will be made available.
